findings.message: verify=False disables TLS certificate validation on a payment request, allowing man-in-the-middle interception of card tokens and charge data.
The charge request has no timeout, so a stalled gateway can hang the caller indefinitely and exhaust threads/workers.
The charge POST has no idempotency key and no safe retry handling, so a timeout or retry can result in duplicate charges to the customer.
The refund POST has no idempotency key, so retries after a timeout can cause duplicate refunds.
Amount is passed through without validation (type, positivity, currency/units), so floats, negatives or zero could be sent to the gateway.

raise_for_status and resp.json() exceptions (HTTPError, ConnectionError, Timeout, JSONDecodeError) are not handled, and the gateway's error body is lost, making declined vs. failed vs. unknown-outcome charges indistinguishable.
resp.json() is returned without validating the response structure or status, so malformed success bodies propagate to callers.

No authentication (API key/credentials) is sent with the charge or refund requests, which is unusual for a payment gateway and suggests missing authorization or reliance on an unauthenticated endpoint.
Each call uses requests.post without a Session, so no connection pooling or reuse occurs, adding TLS handshake overhead per request.

reviews.raw: [{"line":19,"category":"concurrency","severity":"high","message":"get_or_compute reads and writes self._data without holding self._lock, so it races with get() and clear() (check-then-act), and two threads can both compute and overwrite the same key."},{"line":20,"category":"concurrency","severity":"medium","message":"compute() is invoked without any per-key synchronization, so concurrent callers duplicate expensive computation; and if it is moved under the lock, a slow or re-entrant compute() would block all cache access or deadlock with a non-reentrant Lock."},{"line":21,"category":"concurrency","severity":"medium","message":"self._hits += 1 is a non-atomic read-modify-write performed outside the lock, so hit counts can be lost under concurrent access."},{"line":21,"category":"logic","severity":"medium","message":"A hit is counted unconditionally even when the value was just computed (a cache miss), making the hit counter inaccurate and inconsistent with get()."},{"line":22,"category":"concurrency","severity":"high","message":"Returning self._data[key] after the unlocked check can raise KeyError if clear() runs concurrently between the store and the read."},{"line":16,"category":"logic","severity":"low","message":"get() returns None for a missing key, which is indistinguishable from a cached None value, and misses are never counted."},{"line":19,"category":"logic","severity":"low","message":"If compute() returns None or the key's value is legitimately None, behavior is inconsistent between get() and get_or_compute(); also no exception handling means a raising compute() leaves no entry but still propagates without any cleanup or tracking."}]

findings.message: get_or_compute reads and writes self._data without holding self._lock, so it races with get() and clear() (check-then-act), and two threads can both compute and overwrite the same key.

compute() is invoked without any per-key synchronization, so concurrent callers duplicate expensive computation; and if it is moved under the lock, a slow or re-entrant compute() would block all cache access or deadlock with a non-reentrant Lock.
self._hits += 1 is a non-atomic read-modify-write performed outside the lock, so hit counts can be lost under concurrent access.
A hit is counted unconditionally even when the value was just computed (a cache miss), making the hit counter inaccurate and inconsistent with get().
Returning self._data[key] after the unlocked check can raise KeyError if clear() runs concurrently between the store and the read.
get() returns None for a missing key, which is indistinguishable from a cached None value, and misses are never counted.

If compute() returns None or the key's value is legitimately None, behavior is inconsistent between get() and get_or_compute(); also no exception handling means a raising compute() leaves no entry but still propagates without any cleanup or tracking.

findings.message: os.path.join with an unvalidated filename allows path traversal (../ sequences or an absolute path discards UPLOAD_DIR), enabling reads of arbitrary files.
FileNotFoundError, PermissionError and IsADirectoryError from open() are not handled, so a missing or invalid upload raises an unhandled exception to the caller.
f.read() loads the entire upload into memory at once, which can exhaust memory for large files; streaming or a size limit would be safer.
os.system concatenates an unsanitized filename into a shell command, allowing command injection (e.g. '; rm -rf /') as well as path traversal.
The return status of os.system is ignored, so gzip failures (missing file, disk full, existing .gz output prompting) go unnoticed and the function returns None regardless.
Filenames containing spaces or starting with '-' are mis-parsed by the shell and gzip, causing wrong files to be compressed or options to be injected.
os.listdir raises FileNotFoundError or PermissionError if UPLOAD_DIR is missing or unreadable, and this is not handled; it also lists subdirectories as if they were files.

reviews.raw: [{"line":8,"category":"logic","severity":"high","message":"Negative amounts with zero whole part such as \"-0.50\" parse correctly only via sign detection, but int(whole) of \"-0\" is fine while a bare \"-\" or non-digit input raises an unhandled ValueError, and the fraction digits are never validated (e.g. \"1.-5\" or \"1.5x\" yields wrong values or an obscure exception)."},{"line":6,"category":"logic","severity":"medium","message":"Fractions with more than two digits are silently truncated rather than rounded or rejected (e.g. \"1.999\" becomes 199 cents), losing money without any error."},{"line":8,"category":"error-handling","severity":"medium","message":"Malformed input (empty string, whitespace, thousands separators, \"+\" prefix handled inconsistently, None) is not validated, so callers get raw ValueError/AttributeError; also int() accepts underscores and Unicode digits (e.g. \"1_0\"), allowing unintended formats."},{"line":8,"category":"logic","severity":"medium","message":"A sign embedded in the fraction part (e.g. \"5.-3\" gives int(\"-3\") = -3 and returns 497) is accepted and produces an incorrect amount instead of being rejected."},{"line":20,"category":"logic","severity":"medium","message":"For negative cents, divmod gives a non-negative remainder so the result still sums correctly, but the distribution is skewed (e.g. -5 split in 2 gives [-2,-3]), and non-integer or non-int `parts` (e.g. float) causes a TypeError in range() after the check passes."}]

findings.message: Negative amounts with zero whole part such as "-0.50" parse correctly only via sign detection, but int(whole) of "-0" is fine while a bare "-" or non-digit input raises an unhandled ValueError, and the fraction digits are never validated (e.g. "1.-5" or "1.5x" yields wrong values or an obscure exception).
Fractions with more than two digits are silently truncated rather than rounded or rejected (e.g. "1.999" becomes 199 cents), losing money without any error.

Malformed input (empty string, whitespace, thousands separators, "+" prefix handled inconsistently, None) is not validated, so callers get raw ValueError/AttributeError; also int() accepts underscores and Unicode digits (e.g. "1_0"), allowing unintended formats.
A sign embedded in the fraction part (e.g. "5.-3" gives int("-3") = -3 and returns 497) is accepted and produces an incorrect amount instead of being rejected.

For negative cents, divmod gives a non-negative remainder so the result still sums correctly, but the distribution is skewed (e.g. -5 split in 2 gives [-2,-3]), and non-integer or non-int `parts` (e.g. float) causes a TypeError in range() after the check passes.

findings.message: Bare `except:` swallows all exceptions (including KeyboardInterrupt/SystemExit) and silently returns None, hiding the cause of parse failures; catch specific exceptions (ValueError, KeyError, TypeError) and log.
`data["items"]` is not validated to be a list (and `data` is not validated to be a dict), so a payload like {"id":1,"items":null} or {"id":1,"items":5} is accepted as valid and fails later.
parse_order returns None on any invalid input, but `order["items"]` is subscripted without a None check, raising TypeError for malformed payloads.
len() on an unvalidated `items` value can raise TypeError (e.g., int/None) or return a misleading count (e.g., a string or dict) instead of the number of order items.

findings.message: Membership check against a list inside a loop makes unique_customers O(n^2); use a set alongside the list (or dict.fromkeys) to preserve order with O(n) time.
File is opened without a context manager and never closed, so buffered data may not be flushed and the file handle leaks, especially if an exception occurs during writing.
open() is called without encoding or newline arguments, so output encoding is platform-dependent and on Windows lines are written with \r\n translation, which can produce inconsistent CSV output.

Summing amounts with a default of int 0 and no validation means missing keys or string/float amounts raise KeyError/TypeError, and float currency amounts accumulate rounding errors (Decimal should be used for money).
Slicing order['date'][:10] assumes a string ISO-formatted date and raises TypeError/KeyError on None or datetime values, and silently produces wrong day keys on non-ISO formats.

reviews.raw: [{"line": 14, "category": "concurrency", "severity": "medium", "message": "put() and get() block forever with no timeout, non-blocking option, or close/shutdown mechanism, so worker threads waiting on an empty or full queue can never be stopped cleanly and may hang the program on shutdown."}, {"line": 19, "category": "performance", "severity": "low", "message": "notify_all() on a single shared condition wakes every waiting producer and consumer on each operation (thundering herd); separate not_full/not_empty conditions with notify() would avoid needless wakeups."}]

notify_all() on a single shared condition wakes every waiting producer and consumer on each operation (thundering herd); separate not_full/not_empty conditions with notify() would avoid needless wakeups.

reviews.raw: [{"line":10,"category":"security","severity":"high","message":"SQL built via f-string interpolation of username allows SQL injection; use a parameterized query with ? placeholder."},{"line":8,"category":"resource","severity":"medium","message":"The sqlite3 connection is never closed (and cursor not released), leaking a connection/file handle on every call."},{"line":16,"category":"resource","severity":"medium","message":"sqlite3's 'with connect()' context manager only commits/rolls back and does not close the connection, so connections leak on each call."},{"line":23,"category":"resource","severity":"low","message":"The connection is not closed after the 'with' block (it only manages transactions), leaking a connection per call."},{"line":16,"category":"error-handling","severity":"medium","message":"create_user does not handle sqlite3.IntegrityError (e.g. duplicate username/email) or other DB errors, so callers get raw exceptions with no domain-level handling."},{"line":8,"category":"other","severity":"low","message":"A new connection is opened per call with no timeout configuration or pooling, which can cause 'database is locked' errors under concurrent writers and adds overhead."}]

findings.message: SQL built via f-string interpolation of username allows SQL injection; use a parameterized query with ? placeholder.
The sqlite3 connection is never closed (and cursor not released), leaking a connection/file handle on every call.
sqlite3's 'with connect()' context manager only commits/rolls back and does not close the connection, so connections leak on each call.
The connection is not closed after the 'with' block (it only manages transactions), leaking a connection per call.
create_user does not handle sqlite3.IntegrityError (e.g. duplicate username/email) or other DB errors, so callers get raw exceptions with no domain-level handling.
A new connection is opened per call with no timeout configuration or pooling, which can cause 'database is locked' errors under concurrent writers and adds overhead.
